description: Programmable modulating controller (ramps and soaks): process value, set points, alarms, PID settings, program execution, calibration values and identity registers, over Modbus RTU
source: Controladores Microprocessados Modulantes Programáveis TH 90MP, TH 91MP, TH 92MP, TH 93MP (Manual de Operação), 6ª edição (agosto de 2019)

sources.title: Controladores Microprocessados Modulantes Programáveis, TH 90MP / 91MP / 92MP / 93MP (Manual de Operação)
sources.note: linked in issue #122; chapter Protocolo de Comunicação MODBUS RTU, pages 38 to 42

notes: Modbus RTU on the optional RS-485 port. The manual lists registers 40001 to 40105 (function codes 03, 06 and 16, no broadcast); they are numbered from 1 here, so address 40001 is register 1 and address_base is 1. Reading a reserved address returns 0xFFFF. The manual does not name the factory baud rate, parity or controller number: 9600, no parity and 1 are placeholders. Options are 2400, 4800 or 9600 bit/s, no, odd or even parity, 8 data bits and 1 stop bit.

The register table in this edition skips addresses 40025 to 40046 (the page that should list them repeats the first page), so those registers are not included (RP-series controllers have registers there, but the layout may differ).
Values are 16-bit integers, signed where the range includes negative numbers. The manual does not say how decimals are sent: check against the display before applying a scale.

Packed BCD registers (CFPR, SEGP and AL xy) are read in hexadecimal. The relay bit order of register 40007 differs from the TH 9XRP manual. The parity codes (0 = none, 1 = odd, 2 = even) are as printed in this manual, whose label for 0 reads NOME (probably none); the TH 9XRP manual lists even before odd.

Registers 40071 to 40088 act on the segment chosen with PTN and SEGC, and apply only to the programmable series. Registers 40092 to 40099 are calibration values; do not write them without the manual's calibration procedure.

The software version, model number (A and B) and serial number (A, B and C) are plain 16-bit numbers; the manual does not say how they are formed. Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.
